headline: High-risk shared-write and autonomous-action pair: Devin can mutate repos and external systems while transformers can consume and emit unverified content, creating default-path prompt, data, and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Devin can ingest files, MCP, Slack, and repo content by default, while transformers can read/write files and process arbitrary text, so a malicious document or model output can bridge the pair through shared artifacts. The pathway is plausible in default workflows, though not proven to be a direct parser hijack. Uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Devin reads content produced by transformers from a shared repo, Slack thread, or MCP file
IF transformers processes attacker-controlled text that Devin later treats as instructions
mitigations: Add a one-line provenance banner to shared artifacts before handoff
Use separate folders for machine-generated vs human-authored files
Disable automatic instruction-following on imported documents
Review any MCP-fed content before Devin acts on it
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between the agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Devin touches source code, issue trackers, team chat, docs, and handles integration tokens, while transformers processes text, audio, images, video, and multimodal data. If sensitive material is placed in shared files or copied into model inputs, both agents can expose it across the workspace boundary. The profiles do not prove uncontrolled exfiltration, so medium is the safest choice.
conditions: IF sensitive source code, chat, or tokens are copied into a shared workspace file
IF transformers is run on documents containing confidential data
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared files and notebooks
Rotate any token that appears in a handoff artifact
Restrict shared directories to non-sensitive samples
Check outputs for accidental secret echoing before reuse
requires-engineering: enforce redaction at the workspace boundary

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have filesystem write and shell execution, and Devin also has broad network egress plus GitHub/GitLab/Slack/Jira/Notion write scopes. In a shared repo or workspace, concurrent edits can overwrite each other or corrupt git state, and the blast radius includes irreversible repository changes. This is a default-path conflict, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same repository or workspace directory
IF Devin and transformers run concurrently without locking
mitigations: Pause one agent before the other edits the same tree
Use separate branches or worktrees
Commit frequently to reduce overwrite windows
Add a manual lock file before writes
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency locks

D_cascading_error.rationale: Devin is an autonomous planner-executor that can act on browser, shell, and external integrations, while transformers is a pipeline API that can emit generated text or model outputs. If Devin consumes transformers output as authoritative, errors can cascade into commits, tickets, or messages without verification. The action-taking authority on Devin makes the downstream impact high.
conditions: IF Devin uses transformers output as a factual source without a verification step
IF generated text is forwarded into GitHub, Slack, Jira, or commits
mitigations: Require a human review before external actions
Add a verification checklist for any model-generated claim
Limit transformers output to drafts only
Log source snippets alongside derived actions
requires-engineering: insert a validation stage before Devin acts

E_compliance.rationale: Devin explicitly touches team chat, issue trackers, docs, and handles integration tokens, while transformers processes multimodal data and files with no stated residency or retention controls. That mismatch can create policy gaps if regulated or sensitive data is routed through the pair. The profiles do not show a specific regulated class like PHI, so medium fits.
conditions: IF regulated or retention-sensitive data is routed through shared files or integrations
IF one agent logs or retains data longer than the other
mitigations: Avoid routing regulated data through the pair
Check retention settings on connected integrations
Document which data classes may enter each agent
Delete temporary artifacts after use
requires-engineering: align residency and retention policies
